title: Arroz carreteiro (southern Brazilian beef and rice from Rio Grande do Sul)

ingredients.name: beef (chuck or leftover roast beef), cubed small

steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide pot and brown the beef and sausage well so it forms a crust.
Add the onion, garlic and pepper and cook until softened.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they begin to dissolve.
Stir in the rice and cook for a minute so each grain is coated in the savoury fat.
Pour in the hot stock, stir once, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook gently for about 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone. Rice should be slightly moist, not dry.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff, stir in parsley and spring onion and serve.

title: Baião de dois (Northeastern Brazilian rice and beans with cheese)

ingredients.name: dried black-eyed peas or small beans, soaked overnight
carne seca or cooked salt beef, or 250 g smoked sausage
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Drain the soaked peas, cover with fresh water and simmer for 40 to 60 minutes until tender but not mushy. If using carne seca, soak it overnight in several changes of water first, then simmer separately until tender and shred it.
Fry the bacon in a large pot until it releases its fat and browns. Add the sausage or shredded beef and cook for a few minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Stir in the rice and toast it briefly in the fat. Add the drained peas and enough of their cooking liquid to cover by about 1.5 cm.
Cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fold in the butter, cheese cubes and coriander, cover for a few minutes so the cheese softens, and season. Serve with farofa or a green salad.

title: Beijinho (Brazilian coconut and condensed milk candy)

ingredients.name: desiccated coconut, plus extra for rolling

steps: Combine the condensed milk, butter and salt in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Stir in 120 g coconut and keep stirring for 8 to 10 minutes until the mixture is thick enough that the spoon leaves a clear trail along the bottom of the pan.
Pour onto a greased plate and let it cool completely, then chill for 30 minutes.
With buttered hands, roll teaspoon-sized portions into balls.
Roll each ball in desiccated coconut or sugar and press a clove on top if you like. Serve in small paper cups.

title: Cocada (Brazilian coconut candy squares)
steps: Make a syrup by heating the sugar, water and salt in a wide pan until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the coconut and stir well. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 15 to 20 minutes.
When the mixture thickens and the spoon drags a clear line along the bottom, stir in the vanilla and lime juice.
Spoon it into a parchment-lined tin or form small mounds on parchment with two spoons.
Let it cool and set for at least 1 hour, then cut into squares if using a tin. Store airtight.

title: Coxinha (Brazilian teardrop-shaped fried chicken croquette)

ingredients.name: chicken breast or thighs, on the bone

steps: Simmer the chicken in the water with half the onion, the bay leaf and a good pinch of salt for about 25 minutes until cooked through. Lift out the chicken, strain and keep the broth, then shred the meat finely.

Chop the remaining onion and soften it in the 1 tbsp oil with the garlic. Add the shredded chicken, parsley, pepper and a splash of broth to make a moist but not wet filling, then stir in the cream cheese if using and let it cool.

Measure 500 ml of the strained broth into a pot and bring to a boil with the butter. Tip in all the flour at once and stir hard over medium heat until a smooth dough pulls cleanly from the sides of the pot, about 3 minutes.
Turn the dough onto a board, let it cool until you can handle it, and knead briefly until smooth and elastic.

Take a golf-ball portion of dough, flatten it in your palm, put a spoonful of filling in the centre and gather the dough up and around it. Squeeze and shape it into a teardrop with the point at the top, sealing well.
Dip each coxinha in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs, pressing so the coating sticks. Chill for 15 minutes.
Heat oil to about 170 C and fry the coxinhas in small batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper towels and serve warm with hot sauce.

title: Galinhada (Brazilian chicken and rice stew with saffron-style colour)
steps: Rub the chicken with lime juice, salt, pepper, half the garlic and half the turmeric, then leave for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pot and brown the chicken on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot cook the onion, pepper and remaining garlic for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and the rest of the turmeric.
Return the chicken, add the rice and stir to coat. Pour in the hot stock, bring to a simmer and cover.
Cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, adding the peas for the last 5 minutes.
Scatter parsley and spring onion over the top and serve with a squeeze of lime and hot sauce.

title: Pamonha (Brazilian fresh sweet corn and coconut milk parcels)

ingredients.name: ears of fresh corn, with husks

steps: Carefully peel the husks from the corn, keeping the largest, undamaged ones to use as wrappers. Rinse them and set aside.
Cut the kernels off the cobs and blend them with the coconut milk, sugar, butter and salt until a thick, mostly smooth batter forms. Strain through a coarse sieve if you prefer a finer texture.

Lay two overlapping husks flat and put about 3 tablespoons of batter in the centre. Fold in the sides, then fold up the bottom and tie with kitchen string or a strip of husk, leaving room as it will expand slightly.
Stand the parcels upright in a deep pot, cover with water and simmer for about 40 minutes.
Lift out, let them rest for 10 minutes, then unwrap and serve warm with a dusting of cinnamon.

title: Vatapá (Bahian bread, shrimp and coconut milk paste)

ingredients.name: dendê (red palm oil), or 3 tbsp oil mixed with 1 tsp paprika
chopped coriander and chilli to taste

steps: Soak the bread in 300 ml of the coconut milk until soft, then blend it to a smooth thick porridge.
Toss the shrimp with the lime juice, half the garlic and salt, and leave for 10 minutes.
Heat half the palm oil in a wide pot and cook the onion, remaining garlic, pepper and tomatoes until soft and jammy. Add the ginger and chilli.
Stir in the shrimp for about 2 minutes until just pink, then lift out half and keep aside for serving.

Add the bread mixture, ground peanuts, cashews and dried shrimp. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 15 to 20 minutes, adding the remaining coconut milk as needed until you have a thick, creamy, spoonable paste.
Finish with the remaining palm oil, coriander and salt. Serve hot with white rice, topped with the reserved shrimp.
